subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Tangents to the hyperbola x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 make angles θ₁, θ₂ with the transverse axis of the hyperbola. Show that the point of intersection of these tangents lies on the curve 2xy = k(x² − a²) when tanθ₁ + tanθ₂ = k.

insider_note: This proof is nearly identical in shape to the director-circle proof, except it uses SUM of roots for an angle condition instead of PRODUCT of roots for a perpendicularity condition — point out that contrast to a student revising both together.

steps.label: Set up the tangent through P
steps.margin_note: First mark. Same starting formula as the director-circle proof.
steps.memory_tip: Start every 'tangents through a point' hyperbola proof the same way: tangent-with-slope-m formula, forced through the point.
lines: Let the hyperbola be x²/a² − y²/b² = 1
Let P(x₁, y₁) be a point on the locus.
Tangent with slope m: y = mx ± √(a²m² − b²)
If it passes through P(x₁, y₁):
steps.why: Forcing the general hyperbola tangent to pass through P turns 'a tangent through P' into an algebraic equation relating m to the coordinates of P.
common_mistakes: Using the ellipse tangent formula (+b² under the root) instead of the hyperbola one (−b²).
Substituting P into the hyperbola equation itself instead of into the tangent line equation.

steps.label: Form the quadratic in m
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Squaring removes the root and produces a quadratic whose two roots are the two tangent slopes.
steps.memory_tip: Two tangents from one point means: look for a QUADRATIC whose two roots are their two slopes.
steps.why: Equation (1) is a quadratic in m; its two roots m₁, m₂ are exactly the slopes of the two tangents that pass through P.
common_mistakes: Expanding (y₁ − mx₁)² incorrectly and losing the cross term −2mx₁y₁.
Writing the constant term as (y₁² − b²) instead of (y₁² + b²).

steps.label: Apply the angle-sum condition
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Slope IS the tangent of the angle a line makes with the x-axis, which here is the transverse axis.
steps.memory_tip: An ANGLE-sum condition needs SUM of roots; a PERPENDICULAR condition (as in the director-circle proof) needs PRODUCT of roots.
lines: The tangent slopes are m = tanθ,
m₂ = tanθ₂ are the roots of (1)
steps.why: Slope equals the tangent of the angle a line makes with the x-axis, which here IS the transverse axis, so m₁ + m₂ is exactly tanθ₁ + tanθ₂.
common_mistakes: Using product of roots (needed for a perpendicularity condition, as in the director-circle proof) instead of sum of roots, which is what an ANGLE-SUM condition needs.
Forgetting that 'transverse axis' here just means the x-axis of this hyperbola x²/a² − y²/b² = 1.

steps.label: Conclude the locus
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Substitute the given condition and clear the fraction.
steps.memory_tip: This locus 2xy = k(x²−a²) is a curve through both vertices (x=±a gives y=0) — a useful mental check.
steps.why: Substituting the given condition tanθ₁+tanθ₂=k into the sum-of-roots relation and clearing the fraction gives the locus equation directly.
common_mistakes: Cross-multiplying incorrectly and losing the k on one side.
Writing the final locus with y² instead of the product xy — this locus is not a conic in x² and y² separately.
